title: Keynesian economics
summary: In The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money (1936), the Cambridge economist John Maynard Keynes argued, against the theory that had failed to explain the Great Depression, that total demand from households, businesses and government drives output, and that free markets have no self-balancing mechanism that restores full employment. Keynesians therefore justify government action to steady the economy. Keynes later led Britain's delegation at Bretton Woods in 1944, and his analysis of recessions remains the base of modern macroeconomics.

uncertainty.note: Keynes's The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money was published in February 1936.
